newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks end mixed as focus turns to Washington.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks end mixed as focus turns to Washington.

text.p: Wall Street stocks turned in a mixed performance on Tuesday, with blue chips registering modest gains and technology stocks showing narrow losses as attention fixed on events in the nation's capital.
The Dow rose 27 points to close unofficially at 6833 after spending most of the day mildly lower, only to stage a last-minute program-driven advance.
In general, investors displayed a cautious demeanor, as markets awaited the outcome of the Federal Reserve's two-day interest rate policy meeting, which began in Washington Tuesday.

With the Fed meeting under way and President Bill Clinton scheduled to deliver the State of the Union speech Tuesday night, stocks extended a hiatus from the volatility they displayed during most of January.
"Things really do seem to be in a holding pattern," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
While most sectors experienced little action on the day, there were pockets of activity. Technology stocks weakened as questions arose about growth prospects in the networking sector.
"The networkers have been under pressure," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "Generally speaking there's a lot of nervousness in the group."
Nasdaq's most active list was peppered with networking names that fell victim to the jitters. Xylan Corp tumbled 6-1/2 to 22 after reporting earnings that were just shy of estimates.
3Com Corp slipped 3-3/4 to 58-3/4, extending a slide that has taken the shares down about 20 percent during the past two weeks.
The selling pressure spread to networking bellwether Cisco Systems Inc, which reported earnings after the close of trading.

Cisco said it earned $0.49 per share in its fiscal second quarter, up from $0.31 a year ago but a penny shy of First Call's average estimate. After excluding certain write-off charges, the company earned $0.51 per share.
Shares in Cisco, which fell 1-1/8 to 67-1/8 in the regular session, continued falling during after-hours trading, dropping to 65.

Financial stocks were generally strong, with Chase Manhattan Corp up 2-5/8 to 96-3/8 and BankAmerica Corp rising 1-3/8 to 114-5/8. Analysts said the financials took their cue from the bond market, where the yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury dipped to 6.71 percent.
"The bond market appears to be confident about the possibility of a balanced budget amendment," Ackerman said.
"The market will be listening carefully tonight during the State of the Union for signals about progress in balancing the budget," he said.
During the day, leading Republicans in Congress expressed optimism that a balanced budget amendment would win passage in both the House of Representatives and Senate.
In individual issues, Olympic Financial Ltd fell two to 12-5/8 after Oppenheimer & Co started coverage of the shares with a sell rating.

PaineWebber Group Inc rose 3-1/8 to 38-7/8. The company declined to comment as a matter of policy after the NYSE requested a statement regarding the unusual activity in its shares. The firm has been the subject of takeover speculation in recent weeks.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.30 to 1373.75.
The S&P 500 index rose 2.53 to 789.26.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
